[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Human gold-context records for the reference molecules are predominantly below F=20%: aliskiren 2-3%, argatroban lacking or negligible, alvimopan about 6%, melagatran 3-7%, epanolol 6-8%, and tegaserod about 10% fasted.

The only above-threshold F records are species- or prodrug-specific and do not transfer to the query: CDP323 >25% as an ester prodrug in preclinical species and epanolol about 40% in beagle dogs, while human values for those contexts remain 14% and 6-8%.

L4 permeability records for peptide comparators show low intestinal permeability in Caco-2 and in situ systems: hexarelin Caco-2 Papp below detection limit (<1.5e-7 cm/s) and rat SPIP permeability >10-fold lower than enalaprilat; DADLE AP-to-BL Papp 7.8e-8 cm/s with efflux ratios up to 11; FMLP Papp 1.3e-7 cm/s; desmopressin Papp 0.04e-6 cm/s.

L5 gut-wall records show efflux and intestinal metabolism as additional presystemic barriers: MC-LR has very low permeability with apical re-excretion and only 0.3-1.35% reaching basolateral; several compounds show efflux ratios >3; aliskiren gut-formed metabolites account for about 1% of dose.

L6 hepatic-clearance/metabolic-stability records for peptide(-mimetic) comparators show substantial hepatic intrinsic clearance or metabolic instability: saquinavir control CLint 112 ± 28 µL/min/mg (media loss) and 73.8 ± 17.9 (depletion) in rat, with ABT reducing it to 18.0 ± 3.5; KZR-616 HLM CLint 36.5 ± 1.80 µL/min/mg with NADPH and t1/2 76 min; bortezomib metabolism is dominated by CYP3A4 (79% by mAb inhibition). These support that any absorbed fraction of a peptide-like molecule would face significant presystemic/hepatic loss.

The query is far larger and more polar than these comparators (MW 4113 Da, logD -19.42, TPSA 1646 Å², 57 HBD, 56 HBA, neutral fraction 0), so the measured low-permeability and presystemic-loss direction applies a fortiori; no active uptake or prodrug mechanism is identified for this conjugate.

evidence_gaps: No direct measured oral bioavailability value for the query molecule itself.
No matched oral-versus-intravenous exposure data for the query.
No query-specific permeability, efflux, intestinal-metabolism, hepatic-clearance, or metabolic-stability measurement.
No formulation, dose, or prandial-state information for the query.
No data on possible active uptake, prodrug conversion, absorption-enhancer formulation, or specialized oral delivery for the query.
L6 hepatic-clearance records are from other molecules/species/assays; transfer to the query is qualitative only.

The query's extreme size and polarity make F>=20% unsupported.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
